title: Your DNA Is About 2 Meters Long — Inside One Tiny Cell
start_frame_prompt: Ultra-photorealistic vertical cinematic macro of a human fingertip under soft laboratory daylight, realistic pores and skin ridges, shallow depth of field, premium scientific documentary photography, no text, no diagram, no fantasy glow.
negative_prompt: cartoon, infographic, labels, glowing neon DNA, plastic cell, flat medical illustration, text, watermark, black bars, malformed anatomy
narration: Inside almost every nucleated human cell is an astonishing packing problem. If you stretched the DNA from one cell end to end, it would measure roughly two meters. Yet the nucleus is only a few micrometers across. The trick is hierarchical packing. DNA wraps around histone proteins, forming nucleosomes, then folds into increasingly organized chromatin. The molecule is not simply stuffed into a ball. Its three-dimensional organization helps determine which genes are accessible. Two meters of molecular information, folded into a space far smaller than a grain of dust.
captions: ABOUT 2 METERS OF DNA — IN ONE CELL.
THE NUCLEUS IS ONLY MICROMETERS WIDE.

At molecular scale reveal one DNA double helix physically wrapping around histone protein complexes to form nucleosomes. Track along the same molecule as nucleosomes assemble into chromatin. Motion is restrained and physically coherent, water-mediated molecular environment, premium scientific visualization with photoreal material response, no labels or neon colors.

Camera pulls back continuously while following the same chromatin fiber folding into higher-order three-dimensional organization inside the nucleus. Convey immense contour length through scale and repeated folding without showing an impossible telephone-cord chromosome. Preserve molecular continuity; no magical duplication, clipping or arbitrary morphing.

Pull all the way back through nucleus and cell to the original fingertip macro, then briefly hold the exterior human-scale view while a subtle impossible transparent depth cue reveals the tiny nucleus location inside one cell. End with strong scale contrast, realistic skin and laboratory light; no generated text, labels or infographic overlay.

production_notes.director_intent: The reveal is scale: begin human-sized, travel continuously into one cell, follow the same DNA through packing, then return to the fingertip so the two-meter claim feels physically impossible but real.
production_notes.science_guard: Use roughly two meters for DNA in a typical diploid nucleated human cell; do not imply red blood cells contain nuclei or DNA. Avoid outdated rigid 30-nm-fiber claims as universal chromatin structure.
production_notes.sound_design: Natural narration, restrained laboratory room tone at exterior, near-silent intimate molecular ambience without sci-fi zaps.
